sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
sections.content: Briefly revisit superposition and path difference. Explain that coherent light (lasers) maintains a constant phase relationship, which is the foundational requirement for interference.
sections.example: Visualizing two ripples in a pond intersecting to create fixed nodes and anti-nodes.

sections.title: Diffraction: The Bending of Light
sections.content: Define diffraction as the spreading of waves around obstacles. Use Huygens-Fresnel principle to explain how every point on a wavefront acts as a secondary source.
sections.example: Animation showing a laser beam passing through a tiny slit, spreading into a characteristic 'sinc function' intensity pattern on a wall.

sections.title: Holography: Recording the Interference Pattern
sections.content: Explain that while standard photography captures only amplitude (brightness), holography records both amplitude and phase by interfering an object beam with a reference beam.
sections.example: A 3D model of a 'Cyber-Owl' robot: showing the reference beam (direct light) and object beam (reflected light) meeting at the film plate to form complex interference fringes.

sections.title: Reconstruction: The Diffraction Gate
sections.content: Describe the hologram as a 'complex diffraction grating.' When illuminated by the reference beam, the interference fringes diffract light to recreate the original wavefronts, tricking the eye into seeing a 3D image.
sections.example: An animation of a light beam hitting a 'holographic credit card sticker,' where the fringes act as a gate that bends light into the exact shape of the original 3D object.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Summarize that a hologram is essentially a diffraction pattern stored on a medium. Discuss real-world uses in data storage and security.
sections.example: Visualizing a futuristic HUD (Heads-Up Display) in a character's helmet that uses holographic diffraction to project navigation arrows onto the real-world view.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
lecture_lines: Coherent light maintains a stable phase relationship.
Superposition creates fixed interference nodes and anti-nodes.
Path difference between waves determines constructive interference.
animations: #00FFFF: Fade in two circular wave sources on the left side of the screen.
#FF00FF: Animate the waves propagating outward from both centers.
#FFFF00: Highlight the region where crests meet crests (constructive interference).
#00FF00: Highlight the region where crests meet troughs (destructive interference).
#FFFFFF: Fade in labels 'Constructive' and 'Destructive' at the interference points.

storyboard.title: Diffraction: The Bending of Light
lecture_lines: Diffraction is the bending of waves around obstacles.
Huygens-Fresnel principle: each point acts as a source.
Slits cause light to spread into an intensity pattern.
animations: #00FFFF: Display a thin vertical slit on the screen.
#FF00FF: Draw a series of incoming parallel plane waves toward the slit.
#FFFF00: Animate waves emerging from the slit, spreading in a semi-circular pattern.
#00FF00: Display an intensity pattern curve '#00FF00' appearing on a distant vertical wall.
#FFFFFF: Fade in the label 'Diffraction Pattern' above the curve.

storyboard.title: Holography: Recording the Interference Pattern
lecture_lines: Photography captures only brightness, not wave phase.
Holography interferes object and reference beams.
The film records complex phase interference fringes.
Object and reference beams must be coherent.
animations: #00FFFF: Create a 3D model of a 'Cyber-Owl' robot at the center.
#FF00FF: Animate a 'Reference Beam' striking a rectangular plate on the right.
#FFFF00: Animate an 'Object Beam' reflected from the robot to the plate.
#00FF00: Illustrate a complex interference pattern ('Fringes') forming on the plate.
#FFFFFF: Fade in labels: 'Reference', 'Object', and 'Interference Pattern'.

storyboard.title: Reconstruction: The Diffraction Gate
lecture_lines: Holograms act like complex diffraction gratings.
Reference beams hit fringes to recreate wavefronts.
This reconstructs the original 3D optical field.
The observer perceives depth through diffracted light.
Diffraction gates recreate the object's original shape.
animations: #00FFFF: Show the 'Interference Pattern' plate from section 3 on the screen.
#FF00FF: Animate a laser beam (reference) hitting the plate.
#FFFF00: Show diffracted light rays emerging from the plate, converging to form the 3D 'Cyber-Owl' image.
#00FF00: Highlight the plate as a 'Complex Diffraction Grating'.
#FFFFFF: Fade in the label 'Reconstructed Wavefront'.

storyboard.title: Summary & Application
lecture_lines: Holograms are diffraction patterns stored on media.
They enable secure data storage and advanced imaging.
Holographic displays project information onto real-world views.
animations: #00FFFF: Display the 'Cyber-Owl' 3D image floating in the center.
#FF00FF: Animate a light ray traveling through a 'Security Sticker' on a card.
#FFFF00: Illustrate the HUD system projecting arrows onto the scene.
#00FF00: Flash the text 'Holographic Applications: Security, Storage'.
#FFFFFF: Final fade out of all visual components.
